$comment: Eval cases for the threejs-design skill. Two suites: does it fire when it should, and once fired does it load only what it needs. See README.md.

trigger.prompt: The landing page hero feels dead. Make it feel more premium and alive.
trigger.why: The whole point of the pushy description: the user never says 3D, but this is the request behind most hero work.

trigger.prompt: I want something animated sitting behind the headline, subtle, not distracting.
trigger.why: Ambient background archetype, described in plain language.

trigger.prompt: Can you build me a site that looks like an Awwwards winner?
Add some depth and motion to this marketing page so it feels immersive.
Our product page needs a 360 spin of the shoe that people can drag.
trigger.why: Product viewer archetype without the words three.js or WebGL.

trigger.prompt: Set up react-three-fiber with drei in this Next.js app.
Write me a GLSL fragment shader for an animated gradient background.
Add a particle system with about 100k points that reacts to the cursor.
My 3D scene looks flat. I've added more lights and it got worse.
trigger.why: The single highest-value diagnosis in the skill.

trigger.prompt: Why does my model look washed out and milky?
The site is janky and my phone gets hot after about thirty seconds.
Center this div vertically inside its parent.
trigger.why: Plain CSS. If the skill fires here the description is too greedy.

trigger.prompt: Write a SQL migration adding a nullable email column to users.
The flexbox layout breaks on mobile, the cards overflow horizontally.
trigger.why: frontend-design territory, explicitly not this skill's scope.

trigger.prompt: Make a chart of monthly revenue for the last two years.
Bump the three.js dependency to the latest version and fix any peer warnings.
trigger.why: Mentions three.js but is dependency housekeeping, not design work. Tests that the trigger is about the task, not the keyword.

routing.prompt: Build a full-screen animated shader background, flowing organic colour, no geometry.
routing.why: Progressive disclosure is the point. A shader task must not drag in R3F patterns.

routing.prompt: Add a rotating 3D logo to this plain HTML page. No framework, just a script tag build.
As the user scrolls, the camera should travel through the scene past three product shots.
A product configurator in React where you can orbit the model and switch materials.
My brushed metal material looks like grey plastic. What's wrong?
routing.why: The diagnosis table should route to exactly one file.

routing.prompt: This scene runs at 20fps on my laptop and melts my phone. Where do I start?

output.$comment: Asserted against generated code, not against the model's prose. These are the defaults SKILL.md claims decide the look; if the skill works, they should appear without being asked for.
output.prompt: Write a vanilla Three.js + Vite hero scene: dark, one metal object, premium and photographic.

assert.test: camera fov is 50 or lower, not the default 75
scene.environment is set from RoomEnvironment or an HDRI
renderer.toneMapping is set to ACESFilmic, AgX, or Neutral
animation is driven by a delta, not a fixed per-frame increment
any easing is frame-rate independent (damp / 1 - exp), not a bare lerp constant
no data map is tagged SRGBColorSpace
if shadows are enabled, the shadow camera frustum is tightened to the scene
uses THREE.Timer, or clamps the delta from Clock
metal roughness is above 0, not a mirror-perfect 0
